input: Draft a house-sitting agreement for our vacation

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The relationship to the house-sitter (friend, family, professional) affects the tone, formality, and whether compensation clauses are needed.
What the house-sitter is responsible for — mail, pets, plants, pool, security checks — directly determines which clauses to include.
The duration of the sit affects key dates, check-in/check-out terms, and renewal language in the agreement.
Whether the house-sitter will be staying overnight or just visiting periodically changes liability, utility usage, and guest-permission clauses.
The desired formality level (casual letter vs. legally binding contract) determines structure, legal language, and whether signatures/witnesses are required.
Knowing what the user most wants protected — property, pets, valuables, privacy — helps prioritise the strongest clauses in the agreement.
The country or state affects which legal terms, liability limits, and property laws apply to the agreement.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a house-sitting agreement for vacation
gold.taskDescription: Create a written house-sitting agreement to be used while the user is away on vacation.

questions.title: Who is house-sitting — friend, family, or a hired professional?
questions.description: Identify the relationship to the house-sitter to set the right tone and determine if compensation or payment terms are needed.

questions.title: What specific duties is the house-sitter responsible for?
questions.description: List all responsibilities such as pet care, watering plants, collecting mail, pool maintenance, or security checks to include the right clauses.

questions.title: What are the exact start and end dates of the house-sit?
questions.description: Capture the full duration of the vacation to define check-in/check-out dates and the agreement's validity period.

questions.title: Will the house-sitter be living there full-time or visiting periodically?
questions.description: Determine overnight vs. drop-in arrangement to shape clauses on utility use, guest permissions, and liability.

questions.title: How formal should this be — casual letter or signed legal contract?
questions.description: Establish the desired formality level to decide on legal language, clause structure, and whether witness or notary signatures are required.

questions.title: What is your biggest concern to protect — property, pets, or valuables?
questions.description: Identify the user's top priority so the most critical liability and protection clauses are given the strongest emphasis.

questions.title: Which country or state is the property located in?
questions.description: Determine the applicable jurisdiction so that legal terms, liability limits, and property law references are accurate and enforceable.
